findings.reason: At src/renderer.ts:307-324 the switch no longer has a code_inline case, so those tokens hit the default branch and are skipped. default_rules.image (lines 108-109) builds alt from renderInlineAsText, so ![`diagram`](d.png) now renders alt="" instead of alt="diagram". This goes against the docstring's CommonMark rule (strip the markup, keep the content), and the packet has no story asking for the change.
findings.claim: Removing the code_inline case from renderInlineAsText drops code-span text from image alt attributes.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `case 'code_inline':` and its comment `// code content is added as plain text, without backticks` from the switch in `renderInlineAsText`. A code_inline token now falls through to `default: // all other tokens are skipped`. `default_rules.image` (src/renderer.ts:108-109) sets the alt attribute from `slf.renderInlineAsText(token.children!, ...)`. For example, `![run `npm i` now](x.png)` used to render alt="run npm i now" and now renders alt="run  now". The code's own docstring (line 296-297) says the spec requires alt to show the content with the markup stripped, not with the content removed. The packet's acceptance.md names no story asking for this.

findings.reason: A grep of test/ for an image description containing a backtick finds only prose lines in spec.txt and no image-with-code-span example, so no test exercises the removed code_inline path in renderInlineAsText. This is a test gap, so it stays low.
findings.claim: No existing or locked test covers inline code inside image alt text, so the suite can't catch this regression.
findings.evidence: A search of test/ for an image description containing a backtick (`!\[...`...\](`) finds no match. The only other references to code_inline are the renderer rule, smartquotes and backticks.ts, so no test exercises the `renderInlineAsText` code_inline path the diff removes.
